Maria R: Heads-up: profiled 3x mem-spikes on rtx-pool this morning, correlated with KV cache churn + kernel fallback to generic matmul. Samples show warmup hit-rate collapsed from 0.42 -> 0.06 during bursts. attaching quick notes.
Raj P: Sounds like LRU + prefix churn. Proposal: an adaptive 'thermostat' TTL that lengthens TTL for hot prefixes and aggressively shortens cold keys when mem pressure is detected. Bounded footprint and softer eviction curve.
Kenji: Ran a quick canary on dev (6 GPUs). Thermostat params: target_fill=0.78, cool_down=30s. Result: median latency +6% but p99 -18%, evictions -62%. Quick logs: ```before: hit_rate=0.41 evict/s=1223 gpu_mem=14.9GB
after:  hit_rate=0.67 evict/s=450  gpu_mem=15.3GB```
Samir: Nice numbers. Any observable effect on kernel selection or batching jitter?
Maria R: Fewer kernel fallbacks — KV cache reuse reduced sequence-length variance, so kernel-selection traces show ~11% fewer fallback paths. Caveat: increased hotset density required shrinking continuous-batching window from 50ms -> 30ms to keep user p50 < SLO.
Raj P: Safety rules we should add: cap cold_ttl <= 200ms, and a hard mem-limit that flips thermostat into conservative mode (evict-policy=aggressive-lru) if gpu_mem > 0.95 cap. Also probe rate to avoid oscillation.
Kenji: Added runtime probe: `cache.thermostat.probe_every=5s` and metric `cache.thermostat.sigma` for oscillation detection. Early runs show sigma ~0.04 (stable).
perf-bot: perf-regression-bot: Alert 3344556677: p50 increased by 4% on staging after deploying thermostat v1.1 — investigating.
Maria R: :thumbsup: We'll iterate. Next steps: formalize experiment, A/B dashboard (per-key hit-rate, eviction-rate, kernel-fallback-rate), and synthetic burst OOM-safety test. Raj — can you draft rollout plan?
Raj P: On it. Draft plan: canary 5% on dedicated pool, monitor metrics, automatic rollback if evict_rate > baseline*1.5 OR gpu_mem > 0.95 cap. Add a fail-open that disables thermostat if probe oscillation > 0.2.
Kenji: I'll add probe metrics and dashboard widgets. Also saw a small fragmentation spike on smaller GPUs when thermostat extended hot TTLs — we should test slab compaction toggle and per-slab thresholds.
Samir: One more: make thermostat knobs per-pool (dedicated/hosted) not global. Different pools have different memory geometry.
Maria R: Agreed. Final note: thermostat operates on post-canonical keys only — keep prefix key canonicalization upstream unchanged to avoid double-counting hotness.
